decisions.decision: The red criterion is now: the red you hand forward must have RUN and failed, with the failure originating in the code under test rather than in module load, collection or setup. An assertion failure is the sharpest form; a not-implemented throw or an in-body error is valid but blunter; a build or import failure is a prerequisite to clear. Characterization tests are carved out as green by construction.
decisions.rationale: Owner-approved. FOUR owned sources independently decline to require an AssertionError specifically: Clean Code (a build failure IS a legitimate red), Beck (clear the compile error, then run and fail; his own canonical stub throws), Fowler Refactoring 2e Ch.4 (failure versus error, the boundary being an earlier phase), and Meszaros (an error is a legitimate, equally severe red you are told NOT to convert into a failure).

Consequence: the document can carry no markdown link containing a slash, because the three skills' sibling trees differ.

context_notes: SIX of my own errors were caught this session, five of them by the user or by a subagent rather than by my own inspection. (1) I dispatched the executor while the planner was STILL RUNNING, creating a race that nearly cost five real plan requirements -- wait for a planner to return before committing its plan. (2) I invoked three checkers from the wrong workspace and briefly read a module-resolution crash as a gate failure; check-backing, check-crossrefs and check-hygiene live in lz-refactor-workspace, NOT lz-red-workspace -- locate each with find before running. (3) I asserted an unowned RPC etymology and had to retract it; the user's question about GoF is the only reason it was caught before shipping, and it caught it by inverting my own reasoning -- I had excluded GoF BECAUSE it predates the taxonomy, which is exactly what made it worth consulting. (4) I claimed .claude/skills/ is gitignored; the checker is tracked (git check-ignore exits 1). (5) I inferred the placeholder scaffold ban must be narrower than the bare word because the word appears in the tree -- wrong, the ban IS on the bare word and the existing occurrence escapes only because the plural breaks the trailing word boundary. Read the regex instead of inferring from an apparent contradiction. (6) I predicted the book would be materially fuller on Overspecified Software; it is the same single paragraph, so the site reproduced the book's own layout. SEPARATELY the executor found a GUARD THAT COULD NEVER FIRE: a per-line absent regex against a stale marker that WRAPS across two lines reported PASS while the text was fully present. Third false-GREEN of the session. Always verify a new guard FAILS at baseline before trusting it. FINALLY: the taxonomy is 310 lines and I have never read it end to end. I verified it mechanically -- hashes, fences, links, hygiene -- but not substantively. That is precisely what the unbiased review is for, and it is why gates-green must not be mistaken for accepted.
